Scope of service

What we do

Six ways an owner uses us. Every one of them is coordination work: we hold the scope, the drawing, the budget and the programme, and we hold the trades to them.

STR-01

Turnkey holiday home setup

An empty or handed-over unit taken all the way to a furnished, equipped, photograph-ready holiday home — with one person accountable for the whole run.

REF-02

Apartment refurbishment

A tired apartment brought back up — floors, wet areas, joinery, electrics and finishes — planned as one programme instead of a run of separate trades.

INV-03

Property upgrade for investors

A targeted upgrade for a unit that underperforms or sits empty: we work out what actually moves the rate and the reviews, and we leave the rest alone.

FIT-04

STR-ready fit-out

A fit-out designed around how a short-term rental is actually used — durability, storage, cleaning turnaround, and the details guests photograph and mention in reviews.

FFE-05

Furniture, fixtures & equipment

FF&E specified, scheduled, sourced and tracked to a delivery date — including the unglamorous list of equipment a unit needs on day one to operate.

STY-06

Styling & photography readiness

The last mile: styling, dressing and the small corrections that decide whether the photographs sell the unit or quietly undersell it.

Programme

How a project runs

Seven phases. Each line below is written as what you get at the end of it — because that is what you are buying from a project manager.

  1. 01

    Survey and scope

    A measured picture of the unit as it is — not as the original drawings claim — and a written scope that states plainly what is in and what is out.

  2. 02

    Design direction and layout

    A layout and a material direction to approve before anything is priced, so the finished look is a decision you made, not the sum of choices made on site.

  3. 03

    Budget and programme

    A costed scope and a sequence, with the decisions that drive the number set out plainly — so you can see what is expensive and choose whether it is worth it.

  4. 04

    Contractor selection and permits

    Build partners selected and compared on one identical scope, and the approvals route handled — building permits and owners' association requirements included.

  5. 05

    Procurement

    Every item specified, ordered and tracked to a delivery date: finishes, joinery, appliances, furniture, fixtures and equipment, in the order the site needs them.

  6. 06

    Site coordination and quality control

    One point of contact, regular reporting from site, and someone checking the work against the drawing while a correction is still cheap.

  7. 07

    Snagging, styling and handover

    A defects list closed out, the unit styled and cleaned, and a handover so it can be photographed, listed and let without a second round of work.

Who does the building

Licensed contractors and specialist trades. We select them, brief them, hold them to the scope and check the work — we do not carry out the works ourselves.

How long it takes

It depends entirely on scope, unit size, approvals and lead times on the items you choose. We would rather talk it through than publish a number that would be wrong for your project.

What it costs

Also scope-dependent. Bring the property and what you want it to do, and we will tell you what the work involves before anyone talks about a figure.

The commercial case

Why it pays

A renovation on an investment property is a capital decision, not a decorating decision. A unit that is laid out, finished and furnished correctly holds a higher nightly rate, earns better reviews and photographs better — so more of the traffic it already gets turns into bookings.

01 · Rate

What the unit can charge

The rate a unit holds is set by what a guest sees in the first three photographs and what they find when they walk in. Both are decided during the renovation.

02 · Reviews

What guests write afterwards

Reviews punish specifics: the mattress, the shower, the storage, the blackout, the noise. Those are specification decisions taken on a drawing — not fixes you make later.

03 · Conversion

How much traffic converts

A unit that photographs well converts more of the views it already has. Most underperforming listings do not need more traffic; they need a better answer when someone looks.

How this is calculated
  • nights per month30.4 × occupancy = 21.9 nights
  • additional revenue / month(rate after − rate now) × nights per month
  • additional revenue / yearadditional revenue per month × 12
  • simple payback (months)renovation budget ÷ additional revenue per month
  • five-year cumulative uplift(additional revenue per month × 60) − renovation budget
  • net monthly income after(rate after × nights) − monthly operating costs

Operating costs are treated as unchanged by the renovation, so they affect the “net monthly income” line only — never the uplift and never the payback. “Simple payback” means exactly that: it ignores finance costs, taxes, vacancy between bookings, platform fee changes and the time value of money.

This is an estimate, not a forecast. It contains no market data, no assumptions of ours and no promise about your property. It multiplies the numbers you typed. It is not financial advice and it is not a valuation. What a renovation would actually return on your unit depends on the scope, the building, the layout and how the unit is priced and operated afterwards — which is a conversation, not a calculator.

The estimator needs JavaScript to do its arithmetic. The formulas are listed under “How this is calculated” above, and they are simple enough to run on paper. Or send us the five numbers and we will walk through them with you.

Straight answers

Questions we get asked

01Are you a contractor or a project manager?

A project manager. We are not a contracting company and we do not carry out construction work ourselves. We set the scope, direct the design, select and brief licensed contractors and specialist trades, run procurement and approvals, coordinate the site and check the work against the drawing.

The trades do the building. Making sure it is the right work, done properly, in the right order, to an agreed budget and programme — that is the part you are hiring us for.

02What does a project typically involve?

The seven phases set out above: survey and scope, design direction and layout, budget and programme, contractor selection and permits, procurement, site coordination and quality control, then snagging, styling and handover.

How much of that you need varies a great deal. Some owners want everything from first survey to final styling; others already have a contractor and need someone to hold the scope, the budget and the programme so the project does not drift. We would rather scope it against your actual property than describe a “typical” project that may look nothing like yours.

03Do you handle permits and building approvals?

Yes — the approvals route is part of the coordination we run. In Dubai that generally means the building permissions required for the works themselves, plus the requirements of the building's owners' association or developer, alongside the licensing the contractor must hold.

Exactly which approvals apply depends on what you are changing and which building you are in, so we confirm it against your scope before work starts rather than assuming it.

04Can you furnish and equip the unit as well?

Yes. Furniture, fixtures and equipment procurement is part of the service — specification, sourcing, ordering, delivery tracking and installation — including the unglamorous operational equipment a short-term rental needs to work from day one.

Styling and getting the unit ready to photograph are the final stage of the same programme, not a separate project you have to organise afterwards.

05Do you work outside Dubai?

Our work, our own portfolio and our contractor and supplier relationships are in Dubai, and so is our understanding of the approvals. That is where we are genuinely useful.

If your property is elsewhere, ask. The honest answer depends on the location and the scope, and if we are not the right people for it we will say so.

06Who is behind Lux Oasis Interiors & Renovation?

It is operated by Lux Oasis Advisory & Services LLC, TRN 104722180700003 — the same group that runs a DTCM-licensed short-term rental portfolio in JBR, Dubai Marina and Downtown Dubai.

The service exists because we kept doing this work on our own units first: renovating them, furnishing them, handing them over and then operating them. It is a standalone service line, and you can use it on its own.
